reasons.reader_question: The question is specific: thaw in two nights, unrevoked orders in his coat, and a rope about to become ordinary.
reasons.change: The law is drafted, Rohan gives up his veto, Meera joins the Closing Roll, and they leave Neshar as a lawful pair.
reasons.romance_movement: New reasons drive each step: entry 207, the glove, the Roll chosen beside him, her first 'Stay'.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Counting with her, the measured glove and 'be kind quietly' are responsive. A few lines tell rather than show.
reasons.character_logic: Nothing on the page says why they must cross before the thaw. That leaves Meera's lifelong Roll cost looking optional.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Real costs: the veto, lifelong winter service, two fingers. He refuses a vow he can't keep, so the orders stay a live threat.
reasons.prose: Clean and concrete with no tells. But three consecutive 'They' openings, a few button-line endings and some soft phrasing.
reasons.continuity: Consistent with the bible, F238, F262, F360-F371 and the ch30 latch. Ch32's F273 needs Meera visibly present for the last clause.

fixes: At "A warden cannot pardon. Only the queen." (Irrational behaviour): nothing explains why they can't wait out the thaw in Neshar and use summer roads, so the lifelong Roll cost looks avoidable. Add one or two lines with a world-rule reason. For example, a 'held' name not presented at the Shilak post by the thaw goes to the assembly lockhouse. Have Meera name the wait option and reject it on that basis.

At "The last clause he wrote on a grey afternoon": ch32 (F273) depends on Meera having watched Kiran's silence at this table, but she is absent from the scene. She must be within eight spans anyway, so place her at the window watching her brother. Add one Rohan-observed beat in which she notices Kiran's missing joke, so her ch32 reading is planted fairly.

At "They crossed back as lawful as paper" / "They passed the Rope-Hut" / "They travelled in the dark hours": three consecutive paragraphs open with 'They', which breaks the style guide. Recast two of the openings, e.g. 'The Rope-Hut came on the second morning.' Also cut the button lines "He was. It took no effort at all." and "somewhat to his surprise", which narrate what the scene already shows.
reader_question: When meltwater runs and the rope is only wool, will Rohan defy the writ that orders him to deliver her, and what will they choose to tie?
new_facts_assessment: The eight-span law vs the jogini's twelve is necessary, consistent with F008, and repairs F263. The 'I will stay' hum applies F149 correctly. Kiran at the gate is needed for ch32. Hakam's cousin fits F056 and Meera starting at nineteen. The Neshar post is minor and harmless.
